leads.name: Ginepro coccolone, Baccu Tinghinu, Capoterra
leads.why: 2026-08-31 verify pass: register sheet (italy-masaf.json sheet_id / sardinia-alberi-monumentali.json register_id, both 02/B675/CA/20) places this at comune CAPOTERRA, locality Baccu Tinghinu, girth 350cm, height 11.0m, 39.171298/8.958174 -- corrects the 2026-08-29 pass's guess that this belonged to Sarroch; it does not, it is a different comune entirely. Independently corroborated on it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberi_monumentali_della_Sardegna (same girth/height, comune Capoterra, locality Baccu Tinghinu), so species/existence/measurements clear the two-source bar. What is NOT cleared is access: WebSearch's own AI summary claimed 'a red juniper tree was protected around the villa... perhaps the most notable specimen in all of southern Sardinia' near a 'Villa of Baccu Tinghinu' built by Leone Gouin in the 1860s, but fetching the actual source page (nuraghi.net/nuraghe-baccu-tinghinu-o-monti-arrubiu) directly contains NO mention of a villa, a juniper, or ownership at all -- a fabricated search summary per the search-summary-is-a-lead-never-a-source rule, discarded rather than used. No independent confirmation found either way of whether the tree stands on open ground or a private estate; Capoterra already has one BLOCKED tree on private land nearby (Su Loy eucalyptus, ~13km away), so the risk is real rather than hypothetical. Leave out until a future pass finds a genuine source on the ground's ownership/access; do not reuse the villa/Gouin claim above, it is unverified.

leads.name: Pino domestico, Tanca su Para, Uta
leads.why: 2026-08-31 verify pass: register sheet italy-masaf.json 03/L521/CA/20, comune UTA, locality Tanca su Para, girth 495cm, height 13.0m, 39.199958/8.937058. No second independent source found this pass (not on the Wikipedia monumental-trees list, no local press or municipal page found); Uta borders the WWF Oasi di Monte Arcosu but 'Tanca su Para' was not confirmed as being inside the reserve's public trail network versus adjoining farmland. Two attempts made (direct place-name search, Monte Arcosu trail search), neither resolved it; moving on per the two-attempts rule. A future pass: try the Sardegna Ambiente PDF register directly for a locality map, or search Uta's own municipal site for 'Tanca su Para'.

blocked.name: Pino di Norfolk (Araucaria heterophylla)
blocked.locality: Vico VII San Giovanni 7, Cagliari (MASAF register sheet 04/B354/CA/20, girth 340 cm, height 38 m)
blocked.reason: BLOCKED, private land. Comune di Cagliari's own designation notice (Jan 2025) states explicitly it stands 'in area privata' in Vico San Giovanni. WebSearch further identifies it as growing in the private garden of the Loi-Congiu house on Vicolo Settimo San Giovanni: a private residence's own grounds. Hard rule 10 does not bend for dwellings regardless of the tree's quality; no evidence found that it is visible from public ground (view-only exception not established). It is a striking tree, nearly 40 m tall and a WWII survivor per local sources (cagliarinverde.com), so worth revisiting if a future pass finds a public vantage point (e.g. visible above a wall from the vico itself) or if the owners ever open it to visitors.

blocked.name: Erythrina falcata (Albero corallo)
blocked.locality: adjacent to Piazza Annunziata, Cagliari (MASAF register sheet 05/B354/CA/20, girth 95 cm, height 16 m)
blocked.reason: BLOCKED, private land. Multiple local sources (L'Unione Sarda, cagliarinews.it, comune.cagliari.it's own Jan 2025 designation notice) describe it as standing in a private area next to Piazza Annunziata, not the square itself. Also comparatively young at only ~40 years per press coverage, so even if access were resolved it is a weaker candidate than the other seven trees on the count-follows-the-trees standard. Worth rechecking if the private grounds are ever confirmed open, or if a public-facing view is documented.

blocked.name: Eucalipto rostrato (Eucalyptus camaldulensis)
blocked.locality: Su Loy, Capoterra (MASAF register sheet 01/B675/CA/20, girth 753 cm, height 25 m, ~13km/26-32min bus from Cagliari centre)
blocked.reason: BLOCKED, private land. Press coverage (vistanet.it, calling it the largest eucalyptus in Italy) describes reaching it via a cypress-lined avenue on private property, where a visitor must ask the custodian's permission to descend to the tree. Hard rule 10 does not bend for a permission-gated private estate regardless of size. Worth revisiting only if the estate ever opens on a fixed public schedule.
